name: submerged city

attributes.attribute: a city lying under a lake or the sea
called the Land Under the Wave

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The submerged city is a mythic theme found across the Celtic lands. It is the image of a city lying under the water of a lake or the sea. Ireland has such cities: Inchiquin Lough and Lough Gur both hold a drowned town on their rocky floors. Wales keeps the drowned Lowland Hundred of Cardigan Bay below the wave. In Brittany the magical city of Ys rests in the ocean off Pointe du Raz. Some of the drowned cities are homes of the fairy, which is one frame of the place the Celtic otherworld is called the Land Under the Wave. Others were once towns on the surface and went under, either because the people chose to leave this world or because an evil curse fell on them. Beneath the fantasy lies a grain of truth. The Irish Sea, the North Sea, and the Atlantic all hold real sunken ground as the glaciers grew. Memory of drowned land may live in these old tales.
